meta.title: The Brightness Ladder
meta.summary: Eight questions on the order of the seven, the note between each neighbouring pair, the two families and their dials, where the half steps and the tritone fall, and what "brighter" is actually worth.

explanation.text: The principle is how raised the degrees are: Lydian has every degree as raised as it gets, Locrian has the most of them pulled down. Two of the wrong answers are real orderings of something else. The one starting Ionian, Dorian, Phrygian is the conventional listing order — the order you meet the modes walking up a major scale one degree at a time — and it says nothing about brightness. The one starting Ionian, Mixolydian, Lydian is the order listeners actually judged them happiest in, which is the subject of this chapter's last lesson and is not the structural ladder. explanation.text: . The ordering broadly follows the ladder and Lydian is the exception — brightest structurally, third in judged happiness, and two of the three pairs that never reached significance involved it. A second study, in a different lab with a different population, found the same thing. So the honest version of "Lydian is the brightest and happiest mode" is that it is the brightest on the ladder and it is not the happiest in anyone's data. Why the ordering runs this way at all is still unsettled — the pattern is solid, the cause is not.
